entries.question: what turn rate can this plant actually deliver?

turn_rate.note: the commanded cap is ~2x the plant's estimated turn ceiling, and the move+turn slot is infeasible at any commandable speed (walk floor 0.21 m/s => omega <= 0.01 rad/s at r_foot 1.2 m) -- so move+turn is scored relatively and every cap candidate is screened directly instead of probed

entries.question: what is the eval resolution every decision is standardised by, on the per-category suite?

decision_rule.text: STROKE/POSTURE SCREEN: the baseline is B (W + 4000 its of c6y, both stroke/posture knobs at eps, clock-free K in the chain) and every arm (S = the per-foot stroke income at w_S, P = the body-centring bonus at w_P) is judged against B's own screens (control: baseline), never another arm. Every metric is a per-category number of the suite__omni row (summarize()['cat'][c]: the median pooled over both hands of a paired category; survival = the category's own-hold survival), computed over each category's 12-s command window. Blocks (95 %, two-sided), wave 2's verbatim: F = turn: facing_closed, yaw_progress; F_mt = move_turn: facing_closed, yaw_progress; T = fwd, side, back, diag: ratio; RIG (10 members) = steps_per_m on fwd, side, back, diag and steps_per_rad on turn (LOWER is better) plus support_feet on fwd, side, back, diag, turn (HIGHER is better); and LEN (new) = side and diag steps_per_m (LOWER is better: a longer step), the mechanism block neither lever pays directly. Each delta is sign x (candidate - control), so z > R is BETTER in every block; z_b = mean_i(delta_i / R_i); BETTER if z > R, WORSE if z < -R, else TIE. Guards (99 %, one-sided; 23, wave 2's): survival on all seven categories (floored at R_binom); move_turn.ratio; ratio@guard on fwd, side, back, diag; foot_slip on fwd, side, back, diag, turn; steps_per_m@guard on fwd, side, back, diag and steps_per_rad@guard on turn; stand.steps_per_s. R_i = max(R_eval,i, R_seed,i) (+ R_binom for the survival guards), R_eval from D00s (X08-c6 vs X08-c4), R_seed from D00bs (B s3 vs s2). NO adopt_requires: the driver's ADOPT = some block BETTER, nothing WORSE, anchored drift OK; REJECT = any block or guard WORSE, or a stage floor on a non-park category. pair_on [adopt]: an s3 ADOPT queues a seed-2 pair; an all-TIE s3 line is paired by the driver itself; the pooled decision is final. FLOORS: W's suite survival (survival_by_hold) - 0.20 per category; a floor on move_turn or diag PARKS AND FLAGS (floor.park_categories, user decision at audit pass 3): the run continues to its screen and the survival guard against B decides. The driver's ADOPT/REJECT is mechanical: the ADOPTION of S is plan decision 5 (pooled s3 + s2: the S manipulation check of decision 9 passed, side stroke_share not lower beyond its MDE, no block or guard WORSE; LEN BETTER reported as mechanism evidence, not required), read by the orchestrator at SA4 from this line plus `replay_stroke_posture.py readout`. FLAGS (stop and ask, never a verdict; every flagged DECISION parks the driver until `ledger_cli ack-flag`): the clock campaign's set, read against B -- turn facing_closed down >= 0.05, move_turn facing_closed down >= 0.10, any category's survival down >= 0.05, any walking speed ratio down >= 0.05; taps up > 25 %; swing_apex down >= 30 %; support_feet down > 10 %; speed-driven; removal verification failed (every arm is clock-free: every HIDE eval shows clock_obs == 0, every stage ends with both clock weights <= 0.001); a park-category floor (floor_park, immediate). At the orchestrator (SA4, offline readout, not driver flags): term income > 25 % of tracking in any category; side knee_cap_frac up > 20 %; the unison/phase flag on S (and C): tripod coherence below its seed band, or roll_rms collapsing, relative to B (SA0 decision 7). WATCH, never scored: as wave 2 (the cadence set, taps, swing_apex, tripod, slip_per_m, six_down_frac, direction_error, cross_track_ratio, heading_final, settle_s, stand.drift_speed, both hands), plus move_turn survival and pitch (W's known forward nose-dive).
